cards: What defines a true (primary) fungal pathogen?
It can invade and grow in a healthy host
What does an opportunistic fungus need to cause disease?
Impaired host defenses
What is thermal dimorphism?
Growing as a mold at 30 C and a yeast at 37 C
Which fungal form grows in the soil?
The mold (hyphae), below 30 C
Which fungal form grows in the body?
The yeast, at 37 C
Which kind of organism do fungi most commonly infect?
Plants
Which host defense matters most against fungi?
Cell-mediated immunity, with phagocytosis and inflammation
Why is reinfection with opportunistic fungi so common?
Long-term immunity does not develop against opportunists
Which fungi spread from person to person?
Dermatophytes and Candida
Which fungal diseases are the most prevalent?
Dermatophytoses
What is the portal of entry for the systemic mycoses?
Inhaled spores (respiratory)
What is the portal of entry for subcutaneous mycoses?
Trauma that inoculates skin or nails
Why does Sabouraud dextrose agar favor fungi?
Its low pH inhibits most bacteria
Why does potassium hydroxide clear a fungal specimen?
It lyses human cells; fungal walls are thicker
What is a germ tube?
A tiny hyphal tube a yeast sprouts in serum
Why are fungal vaccines typically ineffective?
Reinfection is exceedingly common
Which organism produces amphotericin B?
A soil bacterium, Streptomyces
How does amphotericin B act?
It complexes with fungal membrane lipids, causing leakage
Why is amphotericin B toxic to humans?
Fungi and humans are both eukaryotes
Which fungus is the number one critical pathogen on the World Health Organization list?
Cryptococcus neoformans
Which true fungal pathogen is the most common?
Histoplasma capsulatum
Which soil does Histoplasma favor?
Moist, nitrogen-rich soil with bird and bat guano
Is histoplasmosis spread person to person?
No
Which form does Coccidioides take in the lungs?
Spherules containing endospores
Which form does Coccidioides take in soil?
Block-like arthroconidia
Which weather cycle spreads Coccidioides?
Drought, then heavy rain, then windstorms
How do most Coccidioides infections resolve?
Without any treatment
Which fungal lung infection can mimic lung cancer on X-ray?
Blastomycosis
Where does Blastomyces live?
Forest soil, decaying wood and manure
Which is the rarest primary mycosis?
Paracoccidioidomycosis
Why do subcutaneous fungi rarely disseminate?
Blood and visceral temperatures inhibit them
How is sporotrichosis usually acquired?
A puncture wound from a thorn, wood or roots
What is lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis?
A skin nodule that spreads to nearby lymph nodes
Which tissue do dermatophytes infect?
Keratinized epidermis only: skin, hair, scalp, nails
Which three genera are the dermatophytes?
Trichophyton, Microsporum and Epidermophyton
Which tinea is common in children and causes hair loss?
Tinea capitis
Which tinea comes mainly from animals?
Tinea barbae
Where is tinea pedis rare?
Where people usually go barefoot
What can be a portal of entry for tinea unguium?
Nail extensions
What causes tinea versicolor?
Malassezia furfur, a yeast
Which piedra forms black nodules on scalp hair?
Black piedra (Piedraia)
Which is the dominant opportunistic fungal pathogen?
Candida
What does a Candida albicans colony smell like?
Yeasty, like baking bread
What gives a presumptive diagnosis of candidiasis?
Budding yeast cells and pseudohyphae
Why are Candida auris hospital outbreaks hard to eradicate?
Drug resistance, heat resistance, partial disinfectant resistance
Where does Cryptococcus neoformans live?
Soil around urban pigeon roosts
Which stain shows Cryptococcus' capsule?
A negative stain
Which opportunistic infection is most prominent in acquired immunodeficiency syndrome?
Pneumocystis pneumonia
Which drugs treat Pneumocystis pneumonia?
Pentamidine and co-trimoxazole
What do Aspergillus spores form in the lungs?
Fungal balls
Which practice drives azole resistance in Aspergillus?
Agricultural crop spraying
Which two genera cause most mucormycosis?
Rhizopus and Mucor
Which two factors may have contributed to the rise of mucormycosis in India?
Uncontrolled diabetes and injudicious use of respiratory steroids
Which fungus infects eyes through contaminated contact lenses?
Fusarium
Which mycotoxin is hepatotoxic and carcinogenic?
Aflatoxin
Which fungus causes sick building syndrome?
Stachybotrys chartarum
